title: The Shul Endings
kidRule: A 'shul' ending is spelled C-I-A-L or T-I-A-L. Look at the letter just before it: after a vowel it is usually C-I-A-L, as in SPECIAL. After a consonant it is usually T-I-A-L, as in PARTIAL. One famous rule-breaker is INITIAL.
hint: Listen to the 'shul' at the end. There is no S-H in it! Look at the letter just before the ending: is it a vowel or a consonant?
reminder: The 'shul' ending is C-I-A-L (usually after a vowel) or T-I-A-L (usually after a consonant). If your first try did not work, try the other!

check.question: Why does SPECIAL end with C-I-A-L?
check.correctAnswer: The 'shul' ending is usually C-I-A-L after a vowel, and SPECIAL has the vowel E just before it!
distractors: Because words with a P in them can never have a T

words.def: Different from the rest in a good way.
words.sent: Dad made a special breakfast for my birthday.
words.story: This word comes from the Latin word 'species', which means a kind or a sort. Something of its own kind stands out!
words.card: My *special* *spec*tacles let me see invisible unicorns!

words.def: Only some of a thing, not the whole of it.
words.sent: We could see a partial rainbow behind the clouds.
words.story: In a partial eclipse, the moon covers only a piece of the sun, so the sun looks like a cookie with a bite taken out!
words.card: I ate a *partial* pizza and saved the best *part* for my goldfish!

words.def: Liking to be with others and do things together.
words.sent: Dolphins are social animals that swim in groups.
words.story: Elephants are very social animals. They live in family groups led by the oldest mother or grandmother!
words.card: My *social* *soc*ks love to go to parties in pairs!

words.def: Approved by the people in charge.
words.sent: The official winner of the race got a gold ribbon.
words.story: Every state in the United States has its own official bird. Seven different states picked the bright red cardinal!
words.card: The *official* rule is that hats must fall *off* when you giggle!

words.def: The first letter of a name.
words.sent: I wrote my initial on the inside of my boot.
words.story: This word comes from the Latin word 'initium', which means a beginning. That is why it names the letter that begins your name!
words.card: My *initial* is on my m*it*ten so the snowman knows it is mine!

words.def: Made by people instead of by nature.
words.sent: The artificial grass on the field stays green all winter.
words.story: The first artificial satellite was Sputnik 1. It was launched in 1957 and was only about as big as a beach ball!
words.card: The *artificial* flowers in the *art* room never need a drink!

words.sent: Water is crucial for a growing plant.
words.story: This word comes from 'crux', the Latin word for a cross, like a crossroads where you must choose which way to go!
words.card: It is *crucial* to catch every *cru*mb before the ants do!

words.def: So needed that you cannot do without it.
words.sent: A warm coat is essential on a snowy day.
words.story: Water is essential for every living thing. More than half of your own body is water!
words.card: Grandma *sent* the *essential* camping gear: forty marshmallows!

words.def: The hidden power to become something great one day.
words.sent: Every tiny seed has the potential to become a tall tree.
words.story: A single acorn has the potential to grow into an oak tree that lives for hundreds of years!
words.card: This little *pot* has the *potential* to hold the world's longest noodle!

words.sent: Fresh air and exercise are beneficial for your body.
words.story: Gardeners call ladybugs beneficial insects. One ladybug can eat thousands of tiny plant-munching bugs in its lifetime!
words.card: *Ben* says naps are *beneficial*, so he takes three a day!
